brief: A stronger-than-expected Democratic showing in state elections revived worries about the AI data-centre build-out (power and water demand, permitting, construction costs); combined with a weak Qualcomm earnings outlook, this drove Thursday 5 November's selloff: the S&P 500 fell 4.4% to 7,354, the Nasdaq 100 fell about 6.4%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.3%, leaving chipmakers near 38% below their June high. Breadth was weak (losers beat gainers 5:1, 84% of turnover in decliners) and roughly $2.8tn of market value was lost, a record above the pandemic-era $2.69tn high. The Nasdaq Composite's 5.52% drop was its eighth >5% fall since 2015; after the prior seven, 6 of 7 bounced the next session, 5 of 7 were lower a week later, and 6 of 7 were higher after three months (+23% average), though the sample is thin. Since 30 June, EPS estimates rose for memory, AI infrastructure and semiconductor stocks while their forward P/E multiples fell. J.P. Morgan's Market Intelligence group cites historically supportive midterm-election seasonality and sees heavy deleveraging and depressed momentum exposure as conditions ripe for an alpha recovery, despite still-crowded tech positioning. Syz expects the AI/data-centre investment cycle to continue given its national-security framing.
